chunks: 3375 - And Ali, peace be upon him, said:
“The guardian of the orphan is in the position of his father; he takes the right of preemption for him if he has an interest in it.”
He, peace be upon him, said: “The absentee has the right of preemption.”

key_terms.أَبِيهِ: his father, whose role the guardian assumes in this matter
key_terms.الشُّفْعَةَ: the right of preemption in shared or adjoining property transactions
key_terms.الْيَتِيمِ: the orphan whose legal and financial interests are to be protected
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: in the position or legal standing of
key_terms.رَغْبَةٌ: interest, desire, or wish to exercise that right
key_terms.لِلْغَائِبِ: for the absent person, indicating the ruling applies despite absence
key_terms.وَصِيُّ: the appointed guardian or executor responsible for the orphan’s affairs

ai.seo_question: Does a guardian take shuf'ah on behalf of an orphan, and does an absent person retain the right of preemption?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning shuf'ah, affirming that the orphan’s guardian acts in the place of the father in securing that right on the orphan’s behalf. It also establishes that the right of preemption is not lost merely because the entitled person is absent.
